title: Extend Ansible with Plugins and Collections
objective: Understand filter plugins, collection anatomy, FQCNs, distribution, and version constraints.

paragraphs: Plugins extend how Ansible connects, filters values, looks up data, caches facts, and performs other engine-level work. A filter plugin is Python code that exposes a transformation to Jinja templates.
Collections bundle plugins, modules, roles, playbooks, documentation, and metadata beneath a namespace and name. Fully qualified collection names make module ownership explicit and avoid collisions.
A galaxy.yml manifest identifies a collection. requirements.yml can constrain versions from Galaxy or Automation Hub; pin compatible ranges and know the configured collection installation paths.
explanation.rule: Use FQCNs in shared automation and constrain collection versions for reproducible installs.

examples.title: Collection Requirement
examples.note: A bounded range accepts compatible updates without crossing a major version.

checks.question: What does an FQCN clarify?
options: The collection that owns a module or plugin

feedback.incorrect: An FQCN includes namespace, collection, and content name.

requirements: Use collections, name, and a bounded version.
